concerns.text: The plan proposes McNemar's test for accuracy (binary outcome) on a within-subjects design with 3 conditions (Baseline, LLM, Rule). McNemar's test is strictly for 2x2 paired tables (2 conditions). It cannot handle 3 conditions or the repeated measures structure across 3 arms. Using it here invalidates the causal claim for H1/H3. A Cochran's Q test (for >2 binary conditions) or a Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) / GLMM with a logit link is required.

The plan specifies a Linear Mixed-Effects (LME) model for speed with the formula `time ~ condition + (1 | participant_id)`. This model assumes normality of residuals and homoscedasticity. Time-to-decision data is typically right-skewed and non-normal. Without a transformation (e.g., log-time) or a robust alternative (e.g., GLMM with Gamma distribution or non-parametric aligned rank transform), the p-values and CIs derived from this LME will be statistically invalid, failing to support H2.

The plan states '12 participants (simulated for CI; real recruitment for study)' and '30 tasks per participant'. For a within-subjects design with 3 conditions, 12 participants yields 36 observations per condition. Power analysis for LME with this N is extremely low for detecting anything but massive effect sizes (d > 1.0). The plan acknowledges 'N=12 is small' but proceeds without a formal power calculation or a justification that the effect size is expected to be large enough to be detectable. This risks a Type II error (false negative), rendering the study unable to answer the research question.

The plan proposes bootstrapping CIs for effect sizes (Odds Ratio, Cohen's d) with 10,000 resamples. While bootstrapping is robust, the plan does not specify the resampling unit. In a within-subjects design, resampling individual observations (rows) breaks the dependency structure (participant ID). The bootstrap must be performed at the *participant level* (resampling participants with replacement) to preserve the within-subject correlation. Resampling rows will produce invalid confidence intervals.
